root.name: Three Knights Opening: Steinitz Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 g6

overview: Black fianchettoes with 3...g6 and White usually opens the centre with 4.d4 exd4 5.Nxd4 Bg7 6.Be3 Nf6. Black gets a sound but slightly passive Modern-style set-up, while White has more space and easy development. Play is open and straightforward.

white_ideas.idea: Open the centre with d4 and recapture with Nxd4
Develop with Be3, Qd2 and Bc4 and aim for a small space edge

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the king's bishop and castle
Challenge the d4 knight with ...Nf6 and ...Nxd4

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after d4 exd4 Nxd4, Black in a fianchetto set-up

character.notes: Black takes a solid fianchetto but gives White the initiative.

soundness.notes: Sound for both sides; Black is slightly worse but safe.

structure.notes: Open: the e- and d-pawns are exchanged early.

approach.notes: A rare Black choice, but a normal sideline.

character.reason: Neither side takes big risks; White has the easier game.

structure.reason: The d- and e-pawns come off and pieces have open lines.
